You know, I'm going to level with most people and say the closest thing we have to a God is the planet itself. I'm not trying to do that whole hippy bullshit either. The planet it over 4.6 billion years old. It has housed multiple forms of life and is in a constant state of change. It provides a miriad of environments suitable for a high diversity of life, and provides for it. It also stresses life, allowing it to grow and develop as the planet ages. It in itself is a generator that provides power to many of the planets processes, and houses cycles essential for life. When that generator goes dark, so does the planet. Tectonic activity ceases and so do many the planets cycles and processes. The ocean currents stagnate, and sedimentary processes practically halt. Fertile crust stops being produced, and many essential minerals stop appearing.

The planet might not have created life, but it certainly bore it, and without any sort of guidance has developed into what it is today. I just appreciate it is all I'm saying. And when you think about how this planet functions you gain a better appreciation for it, when places like Mars literally are the same as earth, but without that same generator. There is not tectonic activity on Mars. It is relatively stagnant, and it without energy it is reasonable to understand and assume why it is a dead planet.

So do I believe in a single God? No, not in the traditional sense. I certainly don't believe there is a being who controls or protects me or anyone from the bad things in life. Coincidence however is a force that exists, even if it on a human level it can seem like just "fate". Life is pain and stress, it should be understandable that the world, even if unintentional, pushes us to try and improve, and this in itself is not a bad thing.

You know, its strange. In times like these I like Futurama's interpretation of God. How accidental life is and how being a "God" is essentially a misfortune event. While I have no way of knowing if the Earth has a consciousness, put in the perspective of Bender being a planet, it is understandable that really the planet has nothing against us or its inhabitants. And that the things we do to it and each other are no fault but our own that we should take responsibility for.

So while I tried my best not to sound like some rambling hippy idiot, know I'm not saying this to tell you to start thinking green, eat vegetables, and smoke weed. Know that a living planet is the closest thing to a God, because it really does provide life, from a scientific point of view. And it truly doesn't give a shit about what we do, where we are when we die, or our faults. It doesn't mean go trashing the place, just quit being so god damn arrogant. Science humbled me, not religion. And the fact that everything I know is simply a drop in the bucket of the wealth of knowledge we can earn makes me shake, and that no matter how old humanity is, we will continue to struggle with life and living, no matter how advanced we are, no matter where we are. And I think we will overcome a lot of our problems before we ultimately disappear, and anything we can do to improve our fitness while reducing our impact is a good thing. Because while we shouldn't destroy humanity, it is equally suicidal to try and right off the human element. Because life is not environementally friendly. It is selfish, it thinks only of itself with no regard to its surrounding. A rampant deer population will destroy an ecosystem because of iits intent to thrive. So as sentient beings, we can overcome this desire to "live at the expense of everything else", and instead start thinking of how we can live with less impact. Living organisms will always have an impact on their environment, there is not changing that. We however can recognize that and reduce it.

So live and provide for humanity and the world. Quit waiting around and appreciate how the Earth actually does provide. Because most people don't know just tectonically how important the planet's activity is. Without it we really would be a dead planet. Most don't realize that life in general is destructive. The planet has gone through several mass extinctions, where most of the planet died and recovered.

We can't anger a God. God doesn't care. And neither should you for that matter. Grow as a bit and appreciate what we as a species can accomplish and have accomplished. We have one life. Don't waste it hoping something else will make it better. It is a hollow dream you will live to your last breath. And it would be a waste of a life.

Mississippi Allows Business to Refuse Service to Gay Couples Based on Religious Beliefs.

Mississippian here. It's about what it sounds like.

Personally I believe it's proper to protect private businesses from being forced to violate their own beliefs. Everybody knows about the fundamentalist Christian bakers who had to bake the gay wedding cakes, for example. But this doesn't feel like that. It's packaged as religious liberty, but nobody here really thinks it's all about protecting the poor downtrodden bakers and florists. It's also about being able to throw gays/trans/whatever out of your business just because you don't like them - whether or not you were being asked to violate any of your own beliefs.

Now, you might think that you should be able to do even that, if you want to. As a libertarian I would find it distasteful but would tend to agree. However, my only point was to shine a little light on how it's seen by the locals where I live and work. They're rather fond of it, and for the wrong reasons.

The bill also protects the Kim Davis types from having to sully their hands with anything gayish. Here's a link to the actual bill.

edit: clarity

But this doesn't feel like that. It's packaged as religious liberty, but nobody here really thinks it's all about protecting the poor downtrodden bakers and florists. It's also about being able to throw gays/trans/whatever out of your business just because you don't like them - whether or not you were being asked to violate any of your own beliefs.

The problem here IS that it's packaged as religious liberty. If they had packaged it under liberty in general I would agree.

A person should be able to refuse someone service for any reason. Religious belief should not be required of a test. In fact, framing it under religious belief just opens it up to being shot down by SCOTUS, because government can't advocate in favor of religion. But if they were to frame the law under general liberty there would be no weaknesses to challenge the law.

Also, what happens when an Atheist wants to refuse service to a gay person? He's not doing it on religious principles, but, still, he might have some moral principle against serving gays and this law does not protect him in the same way it protects religious people.

What happens when a Gay business owner wants to refuse service to straight people, on principle that straights can refuse service to him? This law does not protect him in the same way it protects religious people.

It's a law that creates inequity. It creates an upper class of religious people and a lower class of people who are not religious.
